They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same). ecfa38b3d990.text: 30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts). My second book on AI, Co-Existence, is out today (and you can get it here ), 30 months after the release of Co-Intelligence in early 2024. Looking back across the gap between these books is a good way to get a sense of AI progress. And, thanks to AI, I can describe this progress with some quite lovely charts. Making the charts is itself a good indicator of how far things have come. In the era of chatbots, the era of Co-Intelligence , I would have had to work back-and-forth with an AI in a chat window, guiding it through each new step. 619059630d1f.text: AI Is Getting Good at Math. Here’s Why.. In May, an internal model at OpenAI found a counterexample to Erdős's unit distance conjecture . Open since 1946. Many experts had tried to prove it. OpenAI found a counterexample instead. A month later, OpenAI published a proof of the Cycle Double Cover (CDC) problem , then solutions to ten more open problems by July. And a proof of Navier Stokes in September. Anthropic published a formalization of the fermat's last theorem , and advanced bounds on Reimann's hypothesis . The models are suddenly good at math. 5c33d37c37b5.text: Claude Mods: Flipping the Harness Inside Out. For the last few weeks I’ve used Claude Mods to mold Claude Code to my AI engineering workflow. Claude Code is great out of the box, but every engineering workflow is different. Claude Mods let you make Claude Code yours, in the way you want to pay attention. The “paying attention” part is now the most important thing. In a recent Latent Space post, The Evolution of the Agent Harness , I argued that as models absorb more of the harness into their weights, the part that’s left faces the human. It becomes the Attention Interface : the layer that decides when the agent interrupts you, what it shows you, and which decisions it needs you to make.…

digest.headline: Open‑weight models surge, AI’s market power grows, and compute limits spark fresh debates

debates.title: Open weights challenge closed‑AI dominance
debates.summary: Open‑weight models are rapidly catching up to closed‑source leaders, prompting a shift in competitive dynamics. At the same time, governments in the US and China are moving to tighten controls on frontier AI, adding regulatory pressure.

positions.stance: Flags Kimi K3.1 Pro, noting its imminent open‑weight release and pricing that rivals top closed models

Warns that US and Chinese policy proposals aim to require pre‑approval for frontier AI models, tightening the environment for open‑weight releases

debates.title: Internal AI advantage fuels market expansion
debates.summary: Researchers note that labs keep the most advanced models internal, creating a temptation to leverage that edge in high‑value sectors. Regulators are beginning to consider rules that could curb such market moves, setting up a clash between lab advantage and policy.

positions.stance: Predicts OpenAI and Anthropic may use their internal model lead to enter finance and biotech markets directly
Points out emerging US/China regulatory proposals that could restrict the international sharing of frontier AI models, potentially limiting market expansion

debates.title: Compute scaling meets hardware bottlenecks
debates.summary: AI compute demand continues to outpace semiconductor production, raising concerns about sustainable growth. Software‑level efficiencies and serverless infrastructure are being promoted as ways to stretch limited hardware resources.

positions.stance: Explains that AI’s three‑fold annual compute growth is straining chip fab capacity, even with aggressive production upgrades
Advocates serverless AI infrastructure and compute primitives to avoid over‑provisioning as demand rises
